problem: Inverse design requires finding design parameters that achieve target performance, but standard conditional flow matching is sensitive to arbitrary ordering and scaling of coordinates and labels.
approach: Introduces Diagonal Flow Matching (Diag-CFM) with zero-anchoring that pairs design coordinates with noise and labels with zero, making the learning invariant to coordinate permutations.
contribution: Achieves substantially lower round-trip error than CFM across dimensions up to 784, with order-of-magnitude gains on several benchmarks; provides two uncertainty metrics for selecting best candidates and detecting out-of-distribution targets.

problem: Flow matching on Riemannian manifolds still requires numerically integrating probability-flow ODEs during sampling, limiting efficiency.
approach: Extends MeanFlow to manifolds using parallel transport to define average-velocity fields and derives a Riemannian MeanFlow identity for intrinsic supervision in log-map tangent representation.
contribution: Achieves competitive one-step sampling on spheres, tori, SO(3), and SE(3) with improved quality-efficiency trade-offs and substantially reduced sampling cost.

problem: Generalized linear bandits with endogenous memory have loose regret bounds that don't reflect true performance under non-stationary reward dynamics.
approach: Provides sharpened analysis for linear case recovering sqrt(T) regret, extends to generalized linear models with block-wise algorithm using shrunken confidence bounds.
contribution: Achieves regret bound of Õ(sqrt(mT) + d*sqrt(T) + sqrt(κ)*d²*m^{1/4}*T^{1/4} + κ*d²), with leading term independent of link function curvature.

problem: Reward models in RLHF are vulnerable to reward hacking due to noisy annotations and systematic biases like response length or style.
approach: Proposes Bayesian Non-Negative Reward Model (BNRM) integrating non-negative factor analysis into Bradley-Terry preference models with disentangled instance-specific variables and sparse global factors.
contribution: Substantially mitigates reward over-optimization, improves robustness under distribution shifts, and yields more interpretable reward decompositions than baselines.

problem: Entropic optimal transport in continuous spaces has intractable log-partition terms that make existing approaches either computationally inefficient or require restrictive parameterizations or simulation-based training.
approach: Proposes Variational Entropic Optimal Transport (VarEOT) with exact variational reformulation of log-partition as tractable minimization over auxiliary positive normalizer.
contribution: Enables differentiable learning with stochastic gradients avoiding MCMC simulations; achieves competitive or improved translation quality on synthetic data and unpaired image-to-image translation.

problem: AI-generated text detection suffers from boilerplate token dominance and brittle point estimates that fail under adversarial manipulations.
approach: Proposes Uncertainty detector focusing on informative low-probability tokens via multiscale uncertainty estimation using log-probability averaging and Rényi entropy; extends with conditional independent sampling for Uncertainty++.
contribution: Demonstrates high effectiveness and generalization across seven datasets and sixteen LLMs with robustness to adversarial attacks; code available.

problem: Predictive memory in online video models exacerbates drift under occlusion or rapid motion as inaccurate predictions contaminate internal state leading to identity loss.
approach: Interprets video memory as dynamic latent process; introduces Reliability-Guided Predictive Memory (RPM) with latent world model based on state-space dynamics and reliability-aware fusion policy suppressing unreliable predictions.
contribution: Reduces drift after occlusion and outperforms baselines on visual object tracking; demonstrates transfer to video object segmentation across multiple benchmarks.

problem: Preference-based reward modeling with network-sampled annotators exhibits biased inclusion that correlates with graph centrality, leading to over-representation of structural communities.
approach: Proposes Graph-Preference Learning combining graph-personalized reward model sharing strength across neighbors and graph-balanced aggregation using stabilized importance weights.
contribution: Achieves up to 62% reduction in target-welfare recovery error and 17% reduction in cross-language performance gaps under biased inclusion.

problem: Static refusal direction analysis misses how refusal is constructed across layer-token positions, allowing jailbreaks to suppress terminal signals while upstream patterns persist.
approach: Uses causal tracing to identify Refusal Trajectory sparse upstream activation patterns; proposes SALO (Sparse Activation Localization Operator) lightweight white-box detector on hidden states.
contribution: Improves jailbreak detection across Qwen, Llama, and Mistral models on multiple attack families; identifies limitations of static representation engineering approaches.

problem: Dynamic network representation learning requires stable embeddings across nodes and time, but stability guarantees have remained out of reach for normalized Laplacian operators.
approach: Introduces Unfolded Laplacian Spectral Embedding (ULSE) extending unfolded adjacency spectral embedding to normalized Laplacian operators with explicit stability analysis.
contribution: Proves cross-sectional and longitudinal stability under dynamic stochastic block model; yields dynamic Cheeger-type inequality linking spectrum to conductance.

problem: EEG visual decoding ignores the brain's hierarchical visual processing, failing to model low-level to high-level feature organization.
approach: Proposes ViEEG decomposing stimuli into contour, foreground object, and contextual scene; uses three-stream EEG encoder with cross-attention routing and hierarchical contrastive learning.
contribution: Significantly outperforms previous methods on THINGS-EEG and THINGS-MEG datasets in both subject-dependent and subject-independent settings; enables zero-shot object recognition.

problem: Learning with distribution shift is typically viewed negatively, yet with well-chosen training distribution the shift can make hard computational problems tractable.
approach: Formalizes Positive Distribution Shift perspective where training on alternative distribution D' makes learning computationally easier; connects to membership query learning.
contribution: Shows certain hard function classes become learnable under PDS using standard gradient-based training; computational benefits often outweigh statistical ones.

problem: Text-based person retrieval relies on incomplete single-shot queries and chat-based methods lack direct user interaction with retrieved candidates for effective refinement.
approach: Proposes multimodal interactive person retrieval allowing iterative refinement via visual feedback; introduces MNEMO framework with atomic turn encoding and dialogue memory aggregation modules.
contribution: Achieves substantial improvements in retrieval accuracy and generalization; code and dataset publicly available at github.com/Flame-Chasers/MNEMO.

problem: Verifying research-level mathematics solutions is expensive requiring expert time, yet meaningful solutions should generalize to related problems.
approach: Proposes oracle-free Consequence-Based Utility evaluator that scores solutions by testing their value as in-context exemplars in solving related verifiable questions.
contribution: Outperforms reward models and LLM judges; for GPT-OSS-120B improves Acc@1 from 67.2% to 76.3% and AUC from 71.4% to 79.6%.

problem: Fine-grained vision-language alignment remains limited particularly in non-English settings with weak support for bilingual comprehension.
approach: Introduces FG-CLIP 2 bilingual model with region-text matching, long-caption modeling, and Textual Intra-modal Contrastive loss trained on English and Chinese data including new 12M Chinese region-text dataset.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on 29 datasets across 8 tasks for bilingual fine-grained alignment; releases model, code, and benchmark.

problem: Uniform frame sampling in long-video understanding fails to capture key evidence, and existing agentic thinking-with-videos methods are inefficient with rigid workflows.
approach: Proposes VideoTemp-o3 unified framework jointly modeling video grounding and QA with unified masking mechanism for SFT and dedicated rewards for RL to mitigate reward hacking.
contribution: Achieves remarkable performance on long-video understanding and grounding; develops high-quality long-video grounded QA benchmark.

problem: Strictly equivariant models suffer from runtime overhead while non-equivariant models ignore beneficial symmetries; approximately equivariant models need better efficiency.
approach: Proposes projection-based regularizer leveraging layer-wise orthogonal decomposition into equivariant and non-equivariant components with penalties in spatial and spectral domains.
contribution: Consistently outperforms prior approximate equivariance methods in both performance and efficiency with substantial runtime gains over sample-based regularizers.

problem: DPO applies Bradley-Terry model only after deriving the objective, missing the autoregressive structure that shapes token-level preferences.
approach: Reformulates DPO with explicit autoregressive assumption prior to Bradley-Terry model, deriving Autoregressive DPO (ADPO) with shifted summation outside log-sigmoid.
contribution: Explicitly distinguishes token length and feedback length measures; first to analyze their implications for LLM preference optimization.

problem: Graph foundation models exhibit uneven and sometimes negative transfer across domains due to unknown structural mismatch between graphs.
approach: Uses graphon-based continuous limit to decompose cross-domain output shift into finite-sample approximation and relabeling-invariant domain discrepancy; analyzes positional encoding stability.
contribution: Establishes spectral PE stability guarantees and contrasts eigenvector versus subspace-based PE behaviors; translates theory into data curation guidance for GFM transfer.

problem: GNNs suffer from overfitting and over-squashing; edge deletion regularizes but introduces train-inference misalignment while rewiring improves connectivity without training regularization.
approach: Proposes Random Add-Drop Edge (RADE) stochastic augmentation jointly dropping and adding edges with mini-batch gradient-norm balancing for adaptive rates.
contribution: Provably aligns training and inference; mitigates both overfitting and over-squashing; hyperparameter-free in practice with strong node and graph classification results.

problem: Implicit bias of momentum-based optimizers on neural networks remains poorly understood compared to vanilla gradient descent.
approach: Shows momentum steepest descent algorithms (Muon, MomentumGD, Signum) are approximate steepest descent trajectories under decaying learning rates maximizing corresponding norm margins.
contribution: Proves Adam maximizes ℓ∞ margin and characterizes hybrid norms for Adam-variants; results extend to smooth homogeneous models with corroborating experiments.

problem: Dual-encoder vision-language models fail compositional constraints where similarity scores ignore logical operators like 'and' and 'no'.
approach: Proposes factored inference separating evidence extraction from constraint execution; introduces LCSE training-free method that executes constraints externally using frozen encoders.
contribution: Achieves 85.5% accuracy on FACTOR-Bench versus 73.2% for best fine-tuned baseline; improves NegBench COCO MCQ from 27.2% to 65.2% preserving retrieval performance.

problem: Large vision-language models have significant redundancy enabling layer skipping, but determining when to skip lacks principled criteria.
approach: Proposes unified framework characterizing redundancy conditions for layer pruning via experimentally verifiable notions of redundancy independent of downstream task performance.
contribution: Validates that early and late vision tokens are redundant; framework provides theoretically grounded understanding unifying modern layer-skipping techniques.

problem: Truncated linear regression with unknown survival set remains open beyond Gaussian features despite practical relevance.
approach: Develops novel subroutine for efficiently learning unions of bounded intervals using positive examples under smoothness; achieves poly(d/ε) runtime.
contribution: First algorithm for truncated regression with unknown set running in poly(d/ε) time requiring only sub-Gaussian features; advances positive-only PAC learning theory.

problem: Pretrained robot policies have broad behavioral coverage but lack the refinement needed for complex manipulation tasks.
approach: Proposes Distribution Contractive RL (DICE-RL) framework using selective behavior regularization and value-guided action selection to finetune diffusion/flow policies via stable off-policy RL.
contribution: Reliably improves performance with strong stability and sample efficiency; enables mastery of complex long-horizon manipulation in simulation and on real robots.

problem: Time series foundation models require task-specific fine-tuning for different analysis tasks despite having strong zero-shot forecasting capabilities.
approach: Presents Zeus unified TSFM with multi-scale Transformer using point-wise tokenization and U-shaped hierarchy; introduces Multi-Objective Temporal Masking supporting heterogeneous tasks.
contribution: Achieves competitive results across five analysis tasks without tuning; improves performance on out-of-domain benchmarks (+8.06%); code available.

problem: LLM-based time series reasoning fails to capture domain-specific patterns and simple objectives dominate learning in mixed-difficulty tasks.
approach: Introduces Pattern-Aware Alignment extracting trend and seasonality patterns; designs task-aware balanced reward harmonizing learning across difficulty levels.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on diverse Time Series Question Answering tasks; demonstrates superior cross-modal understanding and reasoning capability.

problem: Polypharmacology-guided drug design requires satisfying coupled constraints across multiple heterogeneous binding sites, but existing methods model pockets in isolation.
approach: Proposes pocket-structure-centric generative framework with novel protein representation masking ligand-irrelevant residues while modeling backbone geometry and inter-residue spatial proximity.
contribution: Generates valid candidates with significantly improved binding affinities on COVID-19, schizophrenia, and tumor targets compared to state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Vertex-based message passing GNNs are limited in expressivity by the 1-Weisfeiler-Lehman test; edge-based alternatives need theoretical and practical improvements.
approach: Introduces EB-1WL edge-based color-refinement test and EB-GNN architecture passing messages along edges and triangles inspired by triangle-counting algorithm.
contribution: Shows EB-1WL is significantly more expressive than 1WL with complete logical characterization; EB-GNN admits near-linear time/memory and outperforms standard MPNNs.

problem: Neural compression methods operate at fixed points on rate-distortion-perception surface, requiring retraining to target different tradeoffs.
approach: Proposes training-free framework leveraging pretrained diffusion models with reverse channel coding module and score-scaled probability flow ODE decoder.
contribution: Theoretically proves optimal distortion-perception tradeoff under AWGN and optimal RDP function in Gaussian case; demonstrates flexibility navigating ternary RDP tradeoff.

problem: Long-context reasoning in LLMs lacks understanding of which data types are effective and why; few studies analyze structured table data.
approach: Mathematically analyzes tabular dependency structures using mutual information revealing periodic dependencies; proposes TableLong pipeline synthesizing high-quality table data for RL.
contribution: Table data enhances long-context reasoning across benchmarks (+8.24% average) and out-of-domain settings (+8.06%); provides practical guidance for post-training data.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models memorize training data leading to privacy and copyright concerns; existing methods hurt generation quality or require retraining.
approach: Introduces GUARD framework adjusting denoising to guide away from originals via novel cross-attention attenuation mechanism identifying prompt positions requiring attenuation.
contribution: Most robust memorization mitigation method achieving state-of-the-art results across architectures for verbatim and template memorization while improving image quality.

problem: Hamiltonian and underdamped Langevin Monte Carlo introduce asymptotic bias through numerical integration; unadjusted methods outperform but lack automated step size selection.
approach: Establishes relationship between energy change during integration and asymptotic bias; proposes automatic tuning scheme taking user-provided bias tolerance to select step size.
contribution: Rigorously bounds asymptotic bias for Gaussian targets and numerically validates beyond Gaussians; demonstrates practicality on Bayesian inference and statistical physics problems.

problem: Targeted instruction selection for LLM fine-tuning lacks clarity with fragmented methods, unclear baselines, and entangled components preventing actionable guidance.
approach: Systematically analyzes data representation and selection algorithms with controlled comparisons; unifies selection algorithms as approximate distance minimization with generalization bounds.
contribution: Gradient-based representations consistently choose similar subsets predictive of performance; gains diminish at larger budgets; provides foundation for principled data selection.

problem: Time Series Foundation Models contain redundant intermediate layers but understanding their redundancy and its causes remains unclear.
approach: Introduces mechanistic interpretability tools for TSFMs including ablation studies and logit attribution; develops kernel regressor framework explaining redundancy via stable rank of projection matrices.
contribution: Shows all studied models robust to layer ablation; identifies specific heads responsible for degenerate phenomena like motif parroting and seasonality bias.

problem: Extended context lengths in LLMs cause KV cache to grow linearly, exceeding device limits; existing compression methods incur unbounded peak memory and fail in multi-turn conversations.
approach: Introduces EpiCache training-free framework with block-wise prefill and episodic KV compression clustering conversation history into coherent episodes for episode-specific eviction.
contribution: Improves accuracy up to 30% with 4-6× compression; reduces latency and peak memory by 2.4× and 3.7×; spans three LongConvQA benchmarks.

problem: Predicting street-level socioeconomic indicators from street view imagery fails to exploit structured task-relevant signals and label-efficient learning opportunities.
approach: Proposes MetaStreet semi-supervised multimodal framework with semantic-spatial visual encoder, task-aware LLM encoder, and geography-aware graph contrastive learning.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on two cities across three socioeconomic prediction tasks leveraging spatial autocorrelation.

problem: Controlling fidelity-diversity trade-offs in diffusion generation models lacks principled understanding of attention mechanisms' role.
approach: Characterizes pre-softmax attention as associative memory; decomposes into symmetric (energy landscape) and skew-symmetric (circulation) components; derives Hopfield stability measures.
contribution: Establishes meaningful correlations between Hopfield stability and fidelity-diversity trade-offs; proposes controllable knob modulating via circulation dynamics.

problem: Learning unified road representations across cities fails due to spectral misalignment of graph structures across heterogeneous urban layouts.
approach: Proposes CoSpec framework disentangling road networks into shareable low-frequency commonalities and city-specific high-frequency specificities via hierarchical dual-path architecture.
contribution: Bounds Wasserstein distance between city distributions; demonstrates superior generalization over state-of-the-art baselines.

problem: Approximate furthest neighbor search in adaptive query model with adversarial queries lacks robust data structures achieving theoretical guarantees.
approach: Presents first adversarially robust data structure for c-approximate furthest neighbor with query time Õ(min(d*n^{1/c²}, n^{2/c²} + d)).
contribution: Matches n-dependency of oblivious setting for wide parameter ranges; proves oblivious algorithms fail under adaptive attacks via adversarial attack construction.
